title: Corrections to our 3 October update
text: Our 3 October update said NivKode was “launching 2 November”. 2 November is our target for the public release, not a fixed date, and it may move if testing finds issues. The same update described “dyslexia-friendly and colour-blind-safe themes”. NivKode offers reading-font choices, including OpenDyslexic, and colour palettes for colour-blind users and high contrast; we have checked them with automated contrast tests only. Our 6 October update corrected the other claims in that entry.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 review candidate: 6 October update
text: NivKode 0.1.0 is a review candidate. Development continues. Human review, release approval and publication are pending. Our target for the public release is 2 November 2026, and it may move if testing finds issues. The NivKode source code is licensed AGPL-3.0-only but is not public yet.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 RC8 is a review candidate
text: NivKode 0.1.0 RC8 is a review candidate. Release approval and publication are pending. Linux x86_64 install evidence used a fake local provider; it does not establish live-provider acceptance. No Android physical-device acceptance is claimed. The launch target remains 2 November 2026 and may move if testing finds issues. We also corrected our own research records: some ratings we'd labelled as human were made by an AI model. Those results stay inconclusive, and we've tightened our rules so it can't happen again. Honest results matter more than good-looking ones.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 RC6 is ready for testing
text: Superseded by our corrections on 6 and 7 October. NivKode 0.1.0 RC6 is ready for testing: a desktop app alongside the CLI and live terminal view, dyslexia-friendly and colour-blind-safe themes, and free automated tests on every change. Open source (AGPL-3.0), launching 2 November. We also corrected our own research records: some ratings we'd labelled as human were made by an AI model. Those results stay inconclusive, and we've tightened our rules so it can't happen again. Honest results matter more than good-looking ones.
